shortest_path_query: Obstacle tiles are {obstacle_color}. The start tile is {start_color}, and the goal tile is {goal_color}. Using 4-neighbor moves through non-obstacle tiles, find the shortest path length in steps.
Treat the {obstacle_color} tiles as blocked. The start tile is {start_color} and the goal tile is {goal_color}. Determine the shortest path length in steps using 4-neighbor movement.
Using up/down/left/right moves through tiles that are not {obstacle_color}, find the shortest-path length in steps from {start_color} to {goal_color}.
Find the shortest valid path length in steps from the {start_color} start tile to the {goal_color} goal tile, moving only through tiles that are not {obstacle_color} with 4-neighbor movement.
With {obstacle_color} tiles blocked and no diagonal movement allowed, compute the shortest-path step count from {start_color} to {goal_color}.
reachable_target_count_query: Obstacle tiles are {obstacle_color}. The start tile is {start_color}, and the marked target tiles are {target_color}. Using 4-neighbor moves through non-obstacle tiles, how many target tiles are reachable from the start?
Treat the {obstacle_color} tiles as blocked. The start tile is {start_color} and the marked target tiles are {target_color}. Count the targets reachable with 4-neighbor movement from the start.
Using up/down/left/right moves through tiles that are not {obstacle_color}, determine how many {target_color} target tiles can be reached from the {start_color} start tile.
Find how many marked {target_color} target tiles are reachable from the {start_color} start tile when movement is limited to 4-neighbor steps through tiles that are not {obstacle_color}.
With {obstacle_color} tiles blocked and no diagonal movement allowed, compute how many {target_color} targets are reachable from the {start_color} start tile.
unreachable_target_count_query: Obstacle tiles are {obstacle_color}. The start tile is {start_color}, and the marked target tiles are {target_color}. Using 4-neighbor moves through non-obstacle tiles, how many target tiles are not reachable from the start?

Treat the {obstacle_color} tiles as blocked. The start tile is {start_color} and the marked target tiles are {target_color}. Count the targets that cannot be reached with 4-neighbor movement from the start.
Using up/down/left/right moves through tiles that are not {obstacle_color}, determine how many {target_color} target tiles cannot be reached from the {start_color} start tile.
Find how many marked {target_color} target tiles are unreachable from the {start_color} start tile when movement is limited to 4-neighbor steps through tiles that are not {obstacle_color}.
With {obstacle_color} tiles blocked and no diagonal movement allowed, compute how many {target_color} targets are unreachable from the {start_color} start tile.
